notes.meaning: God gave this message to Jesus Christ to show His people what must take place soon. Jesus then sent His angel to explain these truths to His servant John. The word revelation means pulling back a curtain to make hidden things known.

differ.view: Most of the book is still in the future and will happen just before Christ returns. "Soon" means the events will come suddenly once they start, or that they are near in God's timing.
An older Protestant reading holds that the book traces the church's history from John's day to the end of the world.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars hold that nearly all of the book was fulfilled soon after John wrote it. On this view it describes the fall of Jerusalem and Rome's persecution of Christians.

notes.meaning: John faithfully wrote down everything he saw, describing it as God's word and the message of Jesus. He saw himself as an eyewitness giving an honest report of what had been revealed to him. Believers can trust this message because it comes directly from Christ.

God promises a blessing to anyone who reads this prophecy out loud in church and to all who listen and obey it. A prophecy is a message from God that reveals His truth and what will happen in the future. Because God's plans are moving forward, it is important to take His words to heart right away.

John sends greetings of grace and peace to seven churches in the province of Asia. Grace is God's free love and kindness, and peace is the quiet rest that follows it. This blessing comes from God the Father, who rules all time, and from the Holy Spirit, whose fullness is pictured as seven spirits.

differ.view: The seven spirits are seven high angels who stand before God's throne.

notes.meaning: The greeting also comes from Jesus Christ, who spoke God's truth faithfully even unto death. He was the first person raised from the dead never to die again, and He rules over all earthly kings. Out of His deep love, He freed us from our sins through His death on the cross.

Jesus made His people into a kingdom and appointed them as priests before God the Father. A priest is someone chosen to worship God and bring prayers directly to Him. All glory and power belong to Jesus forever because of what He has done.

Jesus will return openly in the clouds of the sky for every human eye to see. Even those who pierced His body and put Him to death will see Him. People across the earth who rejected Him will weep with deep sorrow and dread when He appears to judge.

differ.view: The verse points mainly to Christ coming in judgment on Jerusalem in AD 70, punishing those who rejected Him.

notes.meaning: The Lord God declares that He is the Alpha and the Omega, which are the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet. This means He is the beginning and the end of all things, holding total control over history. He is the almighty ruler who was in the past, is here today, and is coming again.

John describes himself as a Christian brother sharing in the same sufferings, kingdom, and patient endurance as his readers. The Roman authorities sent him into exile on the island of Patmos because he preached God's message about Jesus. Even when facing hard trials, believers remain closely united in Christ.

On the Lord's Day, which is Sunday when Christians gather to celebrate Jesus rising from the dead, the Holy Spirit took hold of John in a vision. He was lifted above his ordinary senses to receive heavenly truth. Suddenly, he heard a loud, piercing voice behind him like a trumpet call.

differ.view: Being "in the Spirit" was not something rare. John was reading, hearing and keeping God's Word in Sunday worship, as any Christian may.

notes.meaning: The trumpet-like voice commanded John to write down what he saw in a scroll and send it to seven specific churches in Asia. These cities formed a standard travel circuit for a messenger carrying a letter. God wanted the entire church to read and learn from this message.

differ.view: The seven churches also picture seven ages of church history, from the apostles to the last days.

notes.meaning: John turned around to see who was speaking to him with such power. When he turned, he saw seven golden lampstands shining in the darkness. Local churches are like golden stands meant to hold up the light of Christ for the surrounding world to see.

Standing right in the middle of the lampstands was Jesus, appearing as the Son of Man. He wore a long robe reaching to His feet and a golden band around His chest, picturing Him as both a High Priest and a King. This showed that Christ is always present with His churches to protect and guide them.

The hair on His head was pure white like wool or snow, showing His eternal nature, wisdom, and holiness. His eyes blazed like fiery flames, meaning He sees through all pretense and knows every secret thought. Nothing can be hidden from His sight.

His feet glowed like bronze refined and heated white-hot in a furnace, showing His pure strength and readiness to judge evil. His voice sounded like the mighty roar of rushing waters, carrying absolute power. When He speaks, everyone must listen.

Jesus held seven stars safely in His right hand, which shows His loving care and defense of church leaders. A sharp two-edged sword came out of His mouth, picturing His powerful word that cuts through lies and executes judgment. His face shone with dazzling light, as bright as the midday sun.

When John saw this glorious sight, he collapsed at Jesus' feet like a dead man from sheer terror. Jesus placed His right hand on him to give him strength and told him not to be afraid. He reminded John that He is the First and the Last, the eternal Lord of everything.

Jesus declared that He is the Living One who truly died on the cross and is now alive forever. Because He conquered the grave, He holds the keys to death and the underworld, which is the realm of the dead. He has complete power over life, so His followers never need to fear death.

Jesus commanded John to write down the entire revelation for the churches. This included the vision he had just seen, the present spiritual state of the seven churches, and the events that would occur afterward. God gave these words so His people would understand both their present trials and their future hope.

Jesus explained the hidden meaning of the vision to John. The seven stars in His hand are the messengers or ministers of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the churches themselves. Christ holds church leaders securely in His hand while each church holds forth His light.

differ.view: The "angel" of each church is its bishop, the chief overseer over the other church leaders.
The "angel" is the pastor of a single congregation, not a bishop over many churches.
The "angels" are real heavenly angels who watch over each church.
